summary: NVFP4 expert rows on the CPU in a declared operation order that a device kernel reproduces bit for bit
implementation_scope: C++20 scalar oracle plus AVX2 and AVX-512F paths selected at run time (cpuid/xgetbv), bitwise equal to the oracle, for 16- or 32-lane halving or sequential reductions over crit's NVFP4 layout with a scale-decode hook, 1-8 tokens per call; CUDA device function for the halving order; exact Python FP32 reference. Expert composition, activations, threading and the CPU share remain engine supplied.

agent_guidance.use_when: Measured dispatch gives the CPU part of an expert-routed step's NVFP4 misses and output must not depend on where an expert ran
agent_guidance.avoid_when: All experts fit on the device, measurement gives the CPU no share on the target machine, or the device kernel's reduction order cannot be declared
provides: A declared row order: lane = k % lanes, fma(round(e2m1 * scale), x, lane), blocks in order, halving or sequential lane reduction, times post
A second product form, block_dot: per block a sequential unscaled dot, then fma(dot, scale, lane) with blocks dealt over the lanes
Scalar oracle and AVX2 / AVX-512F paths bitwise equal to it, chosen by run-time CPU feature detection
Row interleaving that keeps every row's arithmetic and any thread split bit-identical
Standard E4M3 scale decoder and a hook for checkpoint-specific scale encodings
CUDA dot_row_halving<16|32> and dot_row_block<16|32> with explicit rounding intrinsics and a matching shuffle tree
Exact Python FP32 reference using crit's NVFP4 codec
engine_supplies: Expert composition (projections, activation, routing weight) with activations that match bitwise on both processors
A device kernel declaring the same order, checked against the oracle
Its scale decoder and the post factor exactly as the device applies them
Worker threads and a CPU share chosen by measured dispatch on the target machine
preserve: One FP32 rounding per declared operation; no contraction the order does not name
Lane assignment, block order and reduction pairing identical on host and device
Scales decoded to the exact floats the device multiplies by; post applied as the device applies it
The CPU share comes from measurement, never a constant carried between machines or models
adapt: Row interleaving, threading, token batch and scale caching
Additional ISAs that match the oracle bitwise
Additional declared orders added to oracle, SIMD paths, device function and fixtures together

code_files.purpose: Declared order, matrix view, scale-decode hook, ISA selection and dot_rows
Scalar oracle, cpuid/xgetbv feature detection, scale decoding and dispatch
AVX2 + FMA path, bitwise equal to the oracle
AVX-512F path, bitwise equal to the oracle
Device function for the halving order with explicit rounding intrinsics
Exact FP32 reference of the declared order

requires.hardware: Any CPU for the scalar oracle; x86-64 with AVX2+FMA or AVX-512F for the SIMD paths (detected at run time); a CUDA device for the device function. Python 3.11+ for the reference
requires.model: Expert-routed models with NVFP4 block-scaled weights (one 8-bit scale per 16 values) in crit's layout; checkpoint scale encodings through the hook
requires.workload: Decode or short prompt chunks whose misses measured dispatch splits between CPU and device

contract.input: Matrix view (codes, scales, rows, cols a multiple of the lanes, strides), scale decoder, declared order, FP32 activations for 1-8 tokens with a mask, row range and post factor
contract.output: FP32 row values for the masked tokens; bitwise equal across ISAs, thread splits and a device kernel declaring the same order
contract.ownership: Views only; the caller owns weights, activations and outputs for the call
contract.failure: Invalid geometry, order or token count, and an ISA the CPU does not support, throw std::invalid_argument before any output is written
contract.core_boundary: No Core change; engines call it from their own worker pools

dependencies: C++20 standard library; quantized-projections' nvfp4.h codec
CUDA toolkit for the device function and its fixture
Python standard library and quantized-projections' nvfp4.py for the reference

validation.host: Host fixture: AVX2 and AVX-512 bitwise equal to the oracle over 16/32 lanes, both reductions, standard and engine-style scale hooks, 1-8 token masks and 64-4096 columns; thread splits unchanged; agreement with crit::nvfp4::project; different orders change bits; every path reproduces the Python reference's known answers (MSVC/Windows and GCC/Linux). Worked example: exact FP32 reference, scale-hook equivalence
validation.native: CUDA fixture on an RTX 5090: dot_row_halving and dot_row_block match the host oracle and every host ISA on 1408 and 1152 rows (512-4096 columns, 16 and 32 lanes, block tails); a plainly written device loop differs on most. In one MoE engine with checkpoint-specific CSF scales, block_dot rows through the scale hook matched that engine's own device row arithmetic on 20480 rows of real expert weights
validation.performance: One Ryzen 5 9600 thread: about 8 GB/s of weights for one token on AVX-512. In one MoE engine (WSL2) replacing its own AVX-512 rows: token-identical output, decode within 3%, short-prompt first token about 16% slower
